A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniFall, and their supplied pages, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 references supplementary backbone settings, a VideoMAE-Pre table and numerical distance tables that are not included in its PDF. v2 includes Appendix A. This limits comparison of those supplementary details, while the principal revisions are directly assessable.

before.justification: v1 reports original domain-shift analyses, backbone classification experiments in Tables 2–3, and MS-TCN++ segmentation results in Table 4.

after.justification: v2 reports original training-source comparisons, demographic generalization tests, supervised and unsupervised segmentation results, and temporal-completeness analyses in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: v2 introduces controlled Wan 2.2 synthetic-video generation and reports end-to-end VideoMAE-K400 classification, replacing v1's frozen-backbone approach. Supervised segmentation changes from MS-TCN++ to ASQuery. However, v2's end-to-end description is not clearly reconciled with Appendix A.5's classifier operating on extracted features.

E1.justification: The eight staged datasets and OOPS-derived wild corpus are retained under revised names. v2 adds 12,000 synthetic videos with demographic and environmental variation, expands the taxonomy from 10 to 16 classes, reports full-taxonomy wild evaluation beyond v1's binary wild labels, and evaluates cross-age and cross-BMI scenarios.

E2.justification: v1's classification comparison among I3D, VideoMAE-Pre and VideoMAE-K400 is replaced by VideoMAE-K400 training-source comparisons. SigLIP2 enters the feature comparisons, ASQuery replaces MS-TCN++ for supervised segmentation, and Appendix Table 8 adds evaluated TW-FINCH and KMeans baselines.

E3.justification: The staged CS/CV partitions are retained in Appendix A.2. Reported classification settings change from 150 epochs, batch size 256 and learning rate 5e-4 to 50 epochs, batch size 32 and 1e-5. v2 adds single-source, synthetic and combined-source controls and demographic protocols; embedding smoothing changes from 18-feature averages to five-frame means.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-source ablations, cross-age/BMI robustness tests in Figure 7, and temporal trajectory and recovery-completeness analyses in Appendix A.5.1 and Figure 8. Existing domain-shift analyses incorporate synthetic data and SigLIP2. Conversely, v1's qualitative segmentation prediction example becomes an annotation-only illustration in v2 Figure 3.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3.5 newly documents deterministic, hash-based seeding for synthetic attribute selection. This is limited seed information, not evidence of repeated experimental runs. Neither supplied PDF reports confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run variability for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: v1 reports wild Fall F1 of 0.76/0.82 for I3D and 0.34/0.26 for VideoMAE-K400 under CS/CV training. v2 replaces these comparisons with scores of 52.3% for CMDFall training, 61.2%/60.5% for OF-Staged, 64.2% for synthetic and 65.6% for combined training. These are different experimental conditions, not same-setting improvements. New segmentation, demographic and temporal-analysis results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: v1 Section 4.2 explicitly defines capped dataset weights as w_i = min(max_j |D_j| / |D_i|, 20); v2 omits this mathematical specification. Neither version develops theorems or proofs, so the change is limited to removal of a formal training rule.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims a unified staged-to-wild benchmark and identifies differences between frozen representations. v2 makes controlled synthetic data a central contribution and claims synthetic training can match or surpass staged training on wild transfer. The abstract and conclusion also expand the benchmark claim to three domains, 16 classes and privacy-amenable data generation.

C2.justification: v1 explains transfer through I3D's simpler motion representations and transformer overfitting. v2 emphasizes demographic/environmental diversity, synthetic appearance versus staged motion, and differences in recovery coverage. Its limitations newly discuss generator-induced biases and incomplete synthetic realism, extending the retained concerns about wild coverage and deployment privacy.

D1.justification: v2 documents generation prompts and attributes, annotation tooling and review, source permissions, feature extraction, four H100 GPUs and extraction time. Some precise v1 classifier and loss details disappear. Access wording changes from direct dataset/code links to a project page and an Appendix A.5 release-on-acceptance statement; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The review of existing fall datasets remains largely intact. v2 adds references supporting Wan, SigLIP2, ASQuery, VIA and demographic attribute design, while removing the class-balanced-loss and MS-TCN references. These are targeted additions supporting the expanded benchmark rather than a comprehensive restructuring of the prior-work landscape.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around three domains. Experiments are reorganized around training sources, and dataset splits, search details and limitations move into a substantial appendix. This changes the narrative and document organization beyond simply inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 changes the single-column layout to two columns, introduces a three-domain overview, redraws distribution and embedding plots, and reorganizes result tables with colored rankings. It adds demographic and trajectory figures and appendix tables. Figures 9–20 enlarge the existing embedding analysis rather than constituting separate experiments.

improvement.justification: Shared 16-class wild timelines, direct training-source controls and demographic/recovery analyses substantially strengthen the benchmark's ability to investigate generalization beyond v1's backbone-focused evaluation. Generation and annotation documentation makes the expanded benchmark more auditable. These gains outweigh reduced classifier-backbone coverage, although implementation and access descriptions remain unclear. v2 also overstates universal SigLIP2 superiority: Table 6 gives staged-to-wild F1@50 of 20.26 for SigLIP2 versus 26.37 for I3D. The improvement rests on stronger benchmark design and evidence, not cross-version performance gains.
